apparatus.jury_note: The Jury of Award page prints the two names without descriptors; the descriptors are as printed in the Foreword. The Foreword records that a poll of the previous year's exhibitors showed an overwhelming sentiment for an out-of-town jury, and the same procedure was followed for this show.

foreword.author: Clyde H. Burroughs
foreword.notes: The present exhibition of Michigan Artists is the outgrowth of a small local exhibition held at the Detroit Museum of Art in 1910, in which only a few artists (not more than a dozen) were invited to exhibit; it was then decided to make of it an annual jury exhibition open to all resident artists. Until 1928 the annual exhibition was conducted under the joint auspices of the Detroit Institute of Arts and the Scarab Club; the Scarab Club then withdrew from active participation in the management of the exhibition. This year the exhibition registers the names of 143 painters and 19 sculptors, with a total of 231 works. The works in this exhibition are for sale at studio prices (inquire at desk); no prices are printed in the catalogue.

prizes.name: Detroit Museum of Art Founders Society Prize
prizes.terms: The prize of $200 will be used by the Board of Trustees for the purchase of a work by a resident Michigan artist, to become the property of the permanent collection of the Detroit Institute of Arts. Exhibitors who have received this award will not be eligible again for a period of five years.

apparatus.founders_roll_note: The roll is headed 'THE DETROIT MUSEUM OF ART FOUNDERS SOCIETY PRIZE OF $200 HAS BEEN AWARDED TO THE FOLLOWING' and is followed by the note: 'Those having received the Founders Society Award in the five previous years are not in competition.' No winner is listed for 1934; the gap is preserved as printed.
notes: Prize-name variants between the AWARDS table (printed pp. 4-5) and the PRIZE AWARDS FOR 1942 list (printed pp. 5-6): the table's 'Modern Art Prize' (whose text names it the Friends of Modern Art Prize) is awarded as 'The Friends of Modern Art Prize'; the table's 'Etching Prize' is awarded as 'The Print Purchase Prize'; the table's 'Scarab Club Cash Prize' is awarded as 'The Scarab Club Prize'.

The Honorable Mention (Sculpture) appears in the awards list and in the entry annotation for no. 214 but has no entry in the prize table; the list calls it 'Honorable Mention from Sculpture', the entry annotation 'Honorable Mention for Sculpture'.
The awards list prints 'Michael Ursulescu' without the middle initial of the entry heading 'Michael M. Ursulescu'.

No. 70's title is set with a closed-up em dash in the entry ('Pines and Sand—Michigan') and a spaced em dash in the awards list ('Pines and Sand — Michigan'); each is preserved as printed in its own place.
'Samuel Cashman' (Sculpture heading; awards list) against 'Samuel Cashwan' (Founders Society roll, 1937) - both spellings as printed, not normalised.
'Fredrick Simper' as printed in both the entry heading and the awards list.
No. 75 title as printed: 'Companions of the Awaking Spring'.

The three asterisked headings (Raymond George Hitchcock; Sarkis Sarkisian; Samuel Cashman) are consistent with the five-year rule printed in the catalogue: Hitchcock won the Founders Society Prize in 1940, Sarkisian in 1938, Cashwan (as the roll spells him) in 1937 - all within five years of 1942, Sarkisian exactly at the boundary if the five previous years are counted 1937-1941.
